newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Waigel says German SPD can learn from Austria SPOe.
newsitem.headline: Waigel says German SPD can learn from Austria SPOe.

text.p: German Finance Minister Theo Waigel on Saturday held up Austria's ruling Social Democratic Party (SPOe) as an example to Germany's opposition Social Democrats (SPD).

"I wish the SPD would learn from (Austria's Social Democrat Chancellor) Viktor Klima. Germany's Social Democrats are the most backward in Europe," Waigel said in an interview with Vienna daily Kurier.
Waigel, in Vienna to participate in a television show, accused the SPD of refusing to go along with important budget consolidation measures and structural reforms.
"In other countries there is an agreement with the opposition," Waigel said.
The SPD recently pulled out of tax talks with the coalition and is refusing to return to the negotiating table.
Klima, finance minister until his promotion to chancellor at the start of the year, was the architect of an austerity budget that aims to ensure Austrian qualification for a single European currency.
Waigel reiterated that adherence to the Maastricht Treaty's convergence criteria would determine the single currency's timetable and said Germany was doing its utmost to fulfil the criteria.
Klima and Austrian Finance Minister Rdolf Edlinger were due to meet Waigel for talks on Sunday.
